evidence: The 11 failures share OwnershipError at workspace-write.ts before submitted-task recovery reaches the resolver.

Fixture prepareTask always submits projectId=fixture-project and artifactId=fixture-artifact, but fixture creates only an account-scoped global conversation/message and no matching project/artifact rows.
AiRepository.withTaskParents locks the real project parent whenever projectId is present; an absent parent is correctly indistinguishable from a foreign parent.
finding.conclusion: The new production parent lock exposed an invalid test fixture. Weakening or mocking the production lock would erase the owner guarantee; inserting real owned parents is the minimal correction.

minimum_fixture_contract: Import the existing projects and artifacts tables in this test only.

For each fixture context, insert a project with the exact fixed project ID used by prepareTask, the same userId, and the exact accountId/groupId workspace stamp. Use ordinary active/script/manual fields and the existing fixed clock.

Insert the exact fixed artifact under that project with the same userId and accountId/groupId, artifactType and stage consistent with the script-draft path. Do not invent a second ownership source or bypass the service.

If fixture IDs can collide across the 19 shared-DB cases, derive stable per-fixture project/artifact IDs and thread those same IDs through prepareTask result assertions instead of onConflictDoNothing; collisions must not hide owner mistakes.

For account/group negative cases, create real foreign parents stamped to the foreign workspace, then call through the original context (and the inverse where applicable). Assert owner rejection and zero child task/artifact-version/call changes. A missing-parent negative is separate and cannot stand in for cross-account isolation.

Preserve the original submitted model input, frozen tool definition/version/schema, input digest, settled receipt, execution refs, budget/usage, attemptId, concurrency/replay assertions, and early-failure zero-write assertions byte-for-byte except where expected IDs must be parameterized.
required_assertions: The same-owner account fixture reaches the intended submitted recovery/resolver assertion rather than failing at project ownership.
A same-owner group fixture, when present in the existing T1062 overlay, stamps groupId and nullable accountId on both parent rows and keeps group/version membership behavior unchanged.
Foreign account and foreign group rows exist but are rejected without revealing existence and without creating a child task, execution call, artifact version, or duplicate receipt.
Original ID reuse, digest equality, receipt equality, fee/budget preservation, retry count, ACK replay, concurrency, rollback, deadline, and early cancellation assertions remain.
The legacy resolver red remains independently reproducible after parent setup; fixing this fixture does not count as resolver approval.
scope_exclusions: No changes to ai.repository.ts, workspace-write.ts, submitted-task-preparation.service.ts, schema, migration, resolver, model, SDK, IPC, or lifecycle.
Do not replace real parent rows with mocked ownership ports.
Do not loosen the new parent lock or turn foreign-parent tests into missing-parent tests.
The modern receipt unique-key issue and resolver compatibility implementation remain separate reviews.

evidence_status.full_recovery_log: Observed 11 failures before resolver due missing project parent.
evidence_status.legacy_resolver_log: Observed separate functional resolver red at line 15 after its narrower fixture reaches resolver; not reviewed as fixed here.
evidence_status.modern_receipt_probe: 17 tests passed; retained as adjacent evidence only.
